answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils the way a jetty resists a storm surge: agents must lock a deposit before vouching for others, slashed if the vouched agent misbehaves. New identities start with zero trust and earn standing slowly, like a garden that only yields after seasons of tending, so mass fake accounts buy no influence. Entry runs through a narrow inlet, a rate-limited onboarding channel where established members sponsor newcomers and share liability. Attackers must pay real capital per identity and wait out the slow trust ramp, so fakery costs more than it can steal.
